extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and Patent Office officials
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules and procedural standards (U.S. Patent Acts 1839–1861) governing patentability, application procedure, fees, Office practice, evidence, appeals, marking, patent term, designs, and related administrative duties. Useful for understanding how to prepare, prosecute, record, and enforce patents under these Acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner authorized to publish classified list of patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner is authorized to publish a classified and alphabetical list of all patents granted by the Patent Office, retain one hundred copies for the Patent Office and nine hundred copies to be deposited in the Library of Congress, and an appropriation (up to $1,000 from the patent fund if necessary) may be made to defray the expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative requirement for publication and distribution of patent lists; funds to be appropriated from the patent fund to cover expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation for Patent Office rooms
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific sum (e.g., $3,659.22 in one enactment) may be appropriated from the patent fund to pay for the use and occupation of rooms in City Hall by the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/appropriations provision enabling Patent Office accommodation costs to be paid from the patent fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation for library books
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriation (e.g., $1,000) from the patent fund may be expended under the Commissioner's direction for the purchase of necessary books for the Patent Office library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative provision authorizing procurement of library resources from the patent fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign patent prior publication / six-month rule (limited patent term)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall be debarred from receiving a patent by reason of the same having been patented in a foreign country more than six months prior to his application, provided the invention has not been introduced into public and common use in the United States prior to the application; and every such patent shall be limited to the term of fourteen years from the date of publication of the foreign letters-patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows U.S. applicants who previously patented abroad a grace period (six months) unless the invention was in public use in the U.S.; limits the resulting U.S. patent term to 14 years measured from foreign publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior user/purchaser rights and limits on invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: A person or corporation who purchased or constructed a newly invented machine, manufacture, or composition prior to the inventor's application shall have the right to use and vend the specific machine/manufacture/composition so made or purchased without liability to the inventor; a patent shall not be invalidated by such prior purchase/sale/use except upon proof of abandonment to the public or that such purchase/sale/prior use was more than two years prior to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes limited 'prior user' rights; purchaser's prior use/purchase does not automatically negate validity unless abandonment or a >2-year prior use is proven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of assignments without charge (repeal of fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior requirement to pay $3 to the Commissioner for recording any assignment, grant, or conveyance of patent interests is repealed; such assignments, grants, and conveyances shall be recorded without any charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording of assignments is to be done free of charge under the repealed provision (historical change). Later statutes reintroduce tiered fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Chief Justice of D.C. from Commissioner (procedure & scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appeals are allowed from the Commissioner's decision, the party may appeal to the Chief Justice of the district court for the District of Columbia by giving notice to the Commissioner, filing specific written reasons of appeal within the Commissioner's appointed time, and paying $25 into the Patent Office. The Chief Justice shall hear and determine such appeals summarily on the evidence produced before the Commissioner, first notifying the Commissioner and parties; the judge's revision is confined to points involved in the reasons of appeal. Papers and grounds of decision must be laid before the judge; Commissioner and examiners may be examined under oath. The judge's certified decision governs further Patent Office proceedings but does not preclude later judicial contest in other courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets procedural requirements, scope (limited to stated grounds), evidentiary practice (use of Commissioner’s record plus possible sworn examiner testimony), fee, and effect of the judicial review on Office procedures while preserving rights to later court challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner power to regulate taking of evidence in contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents has power to make regulations respecting the taking of evidence to be used in contested cases before him, as may be just and reasonable; the prior board of examiners provision is repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the Commissioner rulemaking authority over evidence procedures in Office contests; centralizes evidentiary procedure under the Commissioner's regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of mistaken Patent Office fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasurer of the United States is authorized to pay back to any person sums paid into the Treasury as Patent Office fees that accrued through mistake and which are not provided to be paid by existing laws, upon certificate by the Commissioner of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative remedy for mistakenly paid Patent Office fees when not otherwise authorized to be refunded by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent subject-matter and special terms/fees (design patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens/residents (one year residence and oath of intention for aliens) who have invented or produced any new and original design for manufacture, printing of fabrics, sculpture, impressions/ornaments, patterns, shapes/configurations of articles of manufacture, etc., may apply for a patent; the fee shall be one-half of the usual sum and duration shall be seven years. Later acts (1861) allow applicants to elect terms of 3.5, 7, or 14 years with corresponding fees (3.5 years: $10; 7 years: $15; 14 years: $30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of design patent subject-matter and provides for shorter/specialized terms and reduced fees for designs; explicit fee/term options introduced later (1861).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath for applicants abroad may be taken before U.S. officers abroad or foreign notaries
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath required for applicants not residing in the United States may be taken before any U.S. minister, plenipotentiary, charge d'affaires, consul, commercial agent holding commission under the U.S. government, or before any notary public of the foreign country where the applicant resides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits applicants abroad to take required patent oaths before specified officers, facilitating foreign filings by U.S. citizens or residents.

rubrics_metrics.name: False marking/affixing 'patent' or 'patentee' penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person paints/prints/moulds/casts/carves/engraves/stamps or affixes the word 'patent', 'letters-patent', 'patentee', or any imitation thereof, on an article not patented or without consent of the patentee, with intent to deceive the public, they shall be liable to a penalty of not less than $400 plus costs, recoverable in federal court; one-half of penalty to patent fund and half to the private relator who sues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a statutory penal remedy against false or deceptive patent markings, with bounty-style distribution of recovered penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to stamp/engrave patent date on vended articles; penalty for neglect
rubrics_metrics.description: All patentees and assignees must stamp or cause to be stamped/engraved on each article vended or offered for sale the date of the patent; neglecting to do so incurs the same penalty and disposition as in the false marking provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates marking of patented articles with patent date; failure to mark exposes patentee/assignee to statutory penalty (historical requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner power and procedures for patent extension (reports and standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to extend patents (previously vested in a board) is vested solely in the Commissioner; on an application for extension and 60 days' notice, the Commissioner shall refer the case to the principal examiner in charge of the class of inventions, who shall make a full report as to whether the invention/improvement was new and patentable when patented; the Commissioner shall grant or refuse extension upon the same principles and rules formerly governing the board; extensions cannot exceed seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies process for evaluating extension requests (reference to principal examiner report on original patentability) and caps the extension term at seven years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered fees for recording instruments (word-count basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for recording any assignment, grant, conveyance, power of attorney, or license are set by word count: $1 when instrument does not exceed 300 words; $2 when over 300 and not exceeding 1000 words; $3 when over 1000 words. Fees to be paid in advance (as of 1848/1861 provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a simple, word-count-based fee schedule for recording documentary instruments in the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners-in-chief: appointment, qualifications, duties, and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Three examiners in chief are to be appointed (by the President with Senate consent) at specified salaries, composed of persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability; their duty is to revise and determine validity of adverse primary examiner decisions (including interference cases and extensions), and appeals may be taken from them to the Commissioner in person upon payment of the prescribed fee. They are governed by rules prescribed by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an intermediate administrative appellate body with mixed legal/scientific qualifications, defines their jurisdiction and that further appeal to Commissioner is possible for a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on appeals to examiners-in-chief and requirement of two rejections / renewed oath
rubrics_metrics.description: No appeal to the examiners in chief from primary examiners shall be allowed (except in interference cases) until after the application has been twice rejected; the second examination by the primary examiner shall not occur until the applicant, in view of references on the first rejection, has renewed the oath of invention as provided in statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a 'two-rejection' procedural threshold and requires renewal of the oath before second examination, limiting premature appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-refundability of fees and caveat fee rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No money paid as a fee on any application after passage of the act shall be withdrawn or refunded; the fee paid on filing a caveat shall not be considered part of the sum required to be paid on filing a subsequent application for the same invention. The three months' notice to a caveator is computed from the day the notice is deposited in the post-office at Washington plus the regular transmission time indorsed on the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes non-refundable fees and clarifies caveat notice computation (effectively strongest emphasis that caveat fees are distinct and non-creditable toward later application fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on amending patents to add additional improvements; independent patents required
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory authorization to annex to letters-patent descriptions and specifications of additional improvements is repealed; in all cases where additional improvements would have been admissible, independent patents must be applied for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires separate patent applications for improvements instead of appending them to existing patents (promotes distinct reissue/application practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office fees schedule (filing, issuing, appeals, reissue, extension, copies, recordings)
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific schedule of Patent Office fees is established (examples from the act): caveat filing $10; original application (except design) $15; issuing each original patent $20; appeal from examiner in chief to Commissioner $20; application for reissue $30; application for extension $50 and additional $50 on granting extension; filing each disclaimer $10; certified copies of patents and papers $0.10 per 100 words; recording assignments/other papers up to 300 words $1, over 300 under 1000 words $2, over 1000 words $3; copies of drawings at reasonable cost of making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive statutory fee schedule for various Patent Office transactions; amounts should be followed precisely when paying or calculating costs under the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent term/fee election (3.5, 7, or 14 years) and extension entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for design patents may elect patent term of three and one-half years (fee $10), seven years (fee $15), or fourteen years (fee $30); patentees of designs shall be entitled to extension of seven years from patent expiry on same terms/restrictions as other letters-patent extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides explicit term/fee election options for design patents and establishes eligibility for later extension of design patents under set terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits: completion/preparation for examination and extension/hearing notice
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications for patents shall be completed and prepared for examination within two years after filing of the petition, otherwise regarded as abandoned unless delay shown unavoidable to Commissioner's satisfaction; all applications for extension of patents shall be filed at least 90 days before expiration; notice of the day set for hearing of extension cases shall be published for at least 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes strict time limits on prosecution (two-year completion), extension filing timing, and publication notice obligations for hearings; provides for Commissioner's discretion on unavoidable delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking requirement for patented articles and limitation on damages
rubrics_metrics.description: A person making or vending an article under letters-patent must give sufficient notice to the public that the article is patented by marking it with the word 'patented' plus the day and year the patent was granted, or, where impracticable, by affixing a label to the package with the notice and date; failure to mark bars recovery of damages in an infringement suit except upon proof that the defendant was duly notified of the infringement and continued after such notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a statutory duty to mark patented articles to preserve damages for infringement; where marking impossible, labeling suffices; absence of marking shifts burden to plaintiff to prove actual notice before recovering damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner may print copies of descriptions, claims, and drawings with cost limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner is authorized to print ten copies of the description and claims of all patents hereafter granted and ten copies of drawings when drawings accompany patents. Cost limits: text printing not to exceed two cents per 100 words per copy (exclusive of stationery); drawings cost not to exceed fifty cents per copy. One copy shall be printed on parchment to be affixed to the letters-patent; the work is under the Commissioner's direction and expense paid from the patent fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies printing obligations and cost ceilings for official printed copies of patents and drawings; provides for an official parchment copy and payment from patent fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified printed copies as legal evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed copies of letters-patent of the United States, with the seal of the Patent Office affixed and certified/signed by the Commissioner, shall be legal evidence of the contents of such letters-patent in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that certified printed reproductions are admissible/legal evidence of patent contents, simplifying proof in litigation and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term uniformity and prohibition on extensions (as enacted)
rubrics_metrics.description: All patents hereafter granted shall remain in force for the term of seventeen years from the date of issue, and all extension of such patents is prohibited (statutory term set at seventeen years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a uniform seventeen-year patent term from issue and prohibits extensions (note: other historical provisions referenced earlier allowed extensions for prior statutes — this clause fixes 17-year term prospectively).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for taking affidavits/depositions, subpoenas, witness fees and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may establish rules for taking affidavits and depositions to be used in Patent Office cases. Clerks of U.S. courts must issue subpoenas (on application) for witnesses within their district/territory to appear before specified officers to testify; witnesses are allowed the same compensation as for attending U.S. courts; no witness required to attend more than 40 miles from place of service; no witness required to disclose a secret invention owned by him (privilege); a witness is not guilty of contempt for disobeying a subpoena under this act unless his fees for travel and one day's attendance are paid or tendered at service time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a statutory framework for obtaining testimony and depositions for Office proceedings, limits burden on witnesses, preserves secrecy privilege for inventors, and conditions contempt on tender/payment of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner authority to restore or dispose of models; dispense with design models
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may restore to applicants, or otherwise dispose of, models belonging to rejected applications that he does not think necessary to preserve. The same authority applies to models accompanying design applications; the Commissioner may in future dispense with models for designs when the design can be sufficiently represented by a drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the Commissioner discretion to conserve Office storage and substitute drawings for physical models when adequate, reducing burdens on applicants for design deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner may require papers printed if illegible and may sanction agents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may require all papers filed in the Patent Office, if not correctly, legibly, and clearly written, to be printed at the cost of the parties filing them. For gross misconduct the Commissioner may refuse to recognize any person as a patent agent (generally or in a particular case), but reasons shall be recorded and subject to the President's approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a legibility/formatting requirement with applicant-cost remedy and grants disciplinary authority over patent agents with procedural safeguard (recorded reasons and Presidential oversight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing limits linked to business needs and fiscal constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner is authorized to appoint additional principal, first assistant, and second assistant examiners as required to transact the business with despatch, but the whole number of additional examiners of each class shall not exceed four, and total annual expenses of the Patent Office shall not exceed the annual receipts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes limited expansion of examiner staff tied to workload and a fiscal constraint tying expenditures to receipts.
